arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination. Set to a local directory (e.g. /var/backups) or a
# remote host:path (e.g. backup.example.com:/backups) for rsync.
# Override on the command line for one-off runs:  BACKUP_DEST=/srv/backups ./backup.sh
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup: destination not set. Set BACKUP_DEST (or set DEST below)." >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
    echo "backup: logs/ not found in $(pwd)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

# Copy the tarball to the destination. Supports local dirs and host:path via rsync.
if [ -d "$DEST" ] || printf '%s\n' "$DEST" | grep -q '/'; then
    case "$DEST" in
        *:*:
            # host:path — ship with rsync
            rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"/
            ;;
        *:
            echo "backup: unsupported destination '$DEST'" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        *)
            # local directory
            cp -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"/
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "backup: unsupported destination '$DEST'" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "backed up $BUNDLE -> $DEST/"

text: The case pattern for `host:path` is flawed (a local path with a `/` could also contain `:`). Let me rewrite the copy logic to be unambiguous:

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination. Set to a local directory (e.g. /var/backups) or a
# remote host:path (e.g. backup.example.com:/backups) for rsync.
# Override on the command line for one-off runs:  BACKUP_DEST=/srv/backups ./backup.sh
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"
if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup: destination not set. Set BACKUP_DEST (or set DEST below)." >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

if [ ! -d logs ]; then
    echo "backup: logs/ not found in $(pwd)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

# Copy the tarball to the destination. A destination containing a colon is
# treated as a host:path and shipped with rsync; otherwise it's a local
# directory and the tarball is copied with cp.
case "$DEST" in
    *':')
        rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"/
        ;;
    *)
        cp -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"/
        ;;
esac

echo "backed up $BUNDLE -> $DEST/"
